'''Craig Packer''' (born 1950) is an American [[Behavioral ecology|behavioral ecologist]] and professor in the Department of Ecology, Evolution and Behavior at the [[University of Minnesota]]. He is known for long-term research on [[lion]] behavior, [[ecology]] and [[Nature conservation|conservation]], particularly in the [[Serengeti]] [[ecosystem]] of [[Tanzania]].<ref name=":5">{{Cite book |last1=Packer |first1=Craig |title=The Lion: Behavior, Ecology, and Conservation of an Iconic Species |last2=Rosengren |first2=Daniel |date=2023 |publisher=Princeton University Press |jstor=j.ctv2xqngnz |isbn=978-0-691-21529-7}}</ref> His research has examined social behavior, [[population dynamics]], [[genetics]], [[infectious disease]], [[predator–prey interactions]] and [[human–wildlife conflict]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-03-31 |title=What We Are Reading Today: The Lion: Behavior, Ecology, and Conservation of an Iconic Species |url=https://www.arabnews.com/books-gaming/what-we-are-reading-today-the-lion-behavior-ecology-and-conservation-of-an-iconic-species-2279256 |access-date=2026-10-20 |website=www.arabnews.com |language=en}}</ref> He has also conducted research on [[baboon]] [[social behavior]] and has worked on [[Nature conservation|conservation]] and grassland restoration projects in East Africa.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Packer |first1=Craig |last2=Collins |first2=D. A. |last3=Sindimwo |first3=A. |last4=Goodall |first4=J. |date=1995 |title=Reproductive constraints on aggressive competition in female baboons |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/373060a0 |journal=Nature |language=en |volume=373 |issue=6509 |pages=60–63 |doi=10.1038/373060a0 |pmid=7800039 |bibcode=1995Natur.373...60P |issn=0028-0836|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

Packer founded the [[University of Minnesota]]'s Lion Research Center in 1986 and led the Serengeti and Ngorongoro Lion Project beginning in 1978.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Mokaya |first=Caroline Rothery and Steve |date=2023-08-29 |title=Lions and rural communities in a life-or-death battle for survival |url=https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2023-08-29-lions-and-rural-communities-in-a-life-or-death-battle-for-survival/ |access-date=2026-10-20 |website=Daily Maverick |language=en-ZA}}</ref> His research has contributed to the scientific understanding of lion social organization, reproduction, territoriality, disease and population dynamics, as well as to conservation policies concerning African lions.<ref name="umn">{{cite web|url=https://cbs.umn.edu/contacts/craig-packer-0|title=Craig Packer|work=[[University of Minnesota]]|date=2015|access-date=April 21, 2017}}</ref><ref name="elsa">{{cite web|url=https://www.pbs.org/wnet/nature/elsas-legacy-the-born-free-story-interview-lion-expert-craig-packer/6143/|title=Interview: Lion Expert Craig Packer|work=[[Public Broadcasting Service]]|date=September 6, 2012|access-date=October 15, 2012}}</ref> 

==Biography==
Packer was born in [[Fort Worth, Texas]], in 1950 and attended Eastern Hills High School. He studied [[human biology]] at [[Stanford University]], graduating with a bachelor's degree in 1972. While at Stanford, he travelled to Tanzania and worked as a field assistant to primatologist [[Jane Goodall]] at [[Gombe National Park]], where he studied [[olive baboon]] social behavior.<ref name="umn" />

Packer subsequently studied at the [[University of Sussex]], where he conducted doctoral research on baboons and received a [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] in biology in 1977. His early research examined questions concerning social behavior, male dispersal, cooperation and reproductive competition in primates.<ref name="natgeobio">{{cite web|url=http://www.nationalgeographic.com/explorers/bios/craig-packer/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150427180905/http://www.nationalgeographic.com/explorers/bios/craig-packer/|archive-date=April 27, 2015|title=Craig Packer|work=[[National Geographic Society|National Geographic]]|date=2015|access-date=April 21, 2017}}</ref><ref name="umn" /><ref name="facebook">{{cite web|url=https://www.facebook.com/craig.packer.125/about?lst=100007391379881%3A100000311401636%3A1492749531&section=overview&pnref=about|title=About|first=Craig|last=Packer|work=[[Facebook]]|date=November 3, 2010|access-date=April 21, 2017}}</ref>

== Career ==
Following completion of his doctorate, Packer held a series of research and academic appointments in both the [[United Kingdom]] and the [[United States]]. From 1977 to 1980, he worked as a research associate at the [[University of Sussex]],<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=AAAS Fellow Craig Packer Runs with Lions |url=https://www.aaas.org/membership/member-spotlight/aaas-fellow-craig-packer-runs-lions |website=AAAS}}</ref> and beginning in 1978, he became affiliated with the Serengeti Wildlife Research Institute, where he conducted long-term ecological studies for more than three decades.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Walentik |first=Steve |date=2025-03-10 |title=Biologist Craig Packer highlights conservation efforts aimed at protecting lions during Jane and Whitney Harris Lecture |url=https://blogs.umsl.edu/news/2025/03/10/craig-packer-jane-and-whitney-harris-lecture/ |access-date=2026-03-30 |website=UMSL Daily |language=en-US}}</ref>

He later held a postdoctoral research fellowship at the [[University of Chicago]] from 1980 to 1982, followed by a visiting assistant professorship at the [[University of Illinois at Urbana–Champaign]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=ORCID Craig Packer (0000-0002-3939-8162) |url=https://orcid.org/0000-0002-3939-8162 |access-date=2026-03-30 |website=orcid.org}}</ref> In 1983, he joined the [[University of Minnesota]] as an assistant professor in the Department of Ecology, Evolution and Behavior, where he was promoted to associate professor in 1989 and to full professor in 1994.<ref>{{Cite web |title=How I fell in love with natural history, with Craig Packer {{!}} Princeton University Press |url=https://press.princeton.edu/ideas/how-i-fell-in-love-with-natural-history-with-craig-packer |access-date=2026-03-30 |website=press.princeton.edu |language=en}}</ref>

Packer has held numerous additional academic and research affiliations, including visiting scientist positions at [[University of Oxford]] and the [[Santa Fe Institute]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=Craig Packer {{!}} College of Biological Sciences |url=https://cbs.umn.edu/directory/craig-packer |access-date=2026-03-30 |website=cbs.umn.edu}}</ref> 

He also served as an adjunct professor in the [[University of Minnesota]]'s Department of Medicine and Infectious Diseases and International Medicine Division from 2004 to 2022, and as an adjunct faculty member in its International Center for Global Change beginning in 2008.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=Craig Packer {{!}} The Lion Center |url=https://lioncenter.umn.edu/about-us/craig-packer#:~:text=Founder%20and%20Director,%20Lion%20Center,Dr. |access-date=2026-03-30 |website=lioncenter.umn.edu}}</ref>

From 2006 to 2012, he was co-executive director of Savannas Forever Tanzania, an organization focused on sustainable development and conservation.<ref name="Website-1">{{Cite web |last=Tucker |first=Abigail |title=The Truth About Lions |url=https://www.smithsonianmag.com/science-nature/the-truth-about-lions-11558237/ |access-date=2026-03-30 |website=Smithsonian Magazine |language=en}}</ref> In 2013, he was named a [[National Geographic Explorer]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Explorer Home |url=https://explorers.nationalgeographic.org/directory/craig-packer |access-date=2026-03-30 |website=explorers.nationalgeographic.org |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2015-09-16 |title=This Lion Expert Was Banned From Tanzania for Exposing Corruption |url=https://www.nationalgeographic.com/history/article/150916-book-talk-simon-worrall-craig-packer-lions-serengeti-tanzania-trophy-hunting-africa-conservation |access-date=2026-03-30 |website=History |language=en}}</ref>Between 2014 and 2020, he held positions as Honorary Professor at the [[University of KwaZulu-Natal]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Forum Biographies - Craig Packer |url=https://www.wcs-ahead.org/bios/bio_packer.html |access-date=2026-03-30 |website=www.wcs-ahead.org}}</ref> and Research Associate at Oxford's Wildlife Conservation Research Unit.<ref name=":3" />

He has also been affiliated with the Institute on the Environment at the [[University of Minnesota]] since 2016.<ref name=":1" /> In 2019, he became Scientific Director of the Mara Predator Conservation Program in Kenya, a role he has held through 2025.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web |title=Lion Conservation |url=https://www.catawba.edu/news/all-news/2024/lion-conservation/ |access-date=2026-03-30 |website=Catawba College |language=en}}</ref>

== Research ==

=== Primates ===
Packer's early research focused on the behavioral ecology of [[Primate|primates]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=How I fell in love with natural history, with Craig Packer {{!}} Princeton University Press |url=https://press.princeton.edu/ideas/how-i-fell-in-love-with-natural-history-with-craig-packer |access-date=2026-10-20 |website=press.princeton.edu |language=en}}</ref> At Gombe he studied [[Olive baboon|olive baboons]], including male dispersal, social relationships and cooperation. His doctoral work at the [[University of Sussex]] continued his research on [[baboon]] [[social behavior]].<ref>{{Cite book |last=Packer |first=Craig |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=6r0lEAAAQBAJ |title=Into Africa |date=1996 |publisher=University of Chicago Press |isbn=978-0-226-64430-1 |language=en}}</ref> Some of his early papers addressed [[reciprocal altruism]], male transfer between groups and the evolutionary significance of social behavior.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Packer |first=C. |date=1977 |title=Reciprocal altruism in Papio anubis |url=https://www.nature.com/articles/265441a0 |journal=Nature |language=en |publisher=Nature Publishing Group |volume=265 |issue=5593 |pages=441–443 |doi=10.1038/265441a0 |bibcode=1977Natur.265..441P |issn=1476-4687|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

=== Lion research ===
In 1978 Packer began leading what became the [[Serengeti National Park|Serengeti]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Legends and Legacies of Conservation in Africa |url=https://legendsandlegaciesofafrica.org/serengetilionproject.php |access-date=2026-10-20 |website=legendsandlegaciesofafrica.org}}</ref> and [[Ngorongoro Conservation Area|Ngorongoro Lion Project]],<ref>{{Cite news |last=Goode |first=Erica |date=2015-12-28 |title=A Lion Expert Who Isn't Inclined to Turn Tail |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2015/12/29/science/lions-hunting-africa-craig-packer.html |access-date=2026-10-20 |work=The New York Times |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331}}</ref> establishing a long-term field study of [[African lions]] in [[Tanzania]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=teamAG |date=2020-08-21 |title=Lion trophy hunting - we interview Craig Packer |url=https://africageographic.com/stories/lion-trophy-hunting-we-interview-craig-packer/ |access-date=2026-10-20 |website=Africa Geographic |language=en-US}}</ref> The project continued for more than three decades and became one of the longest-running studies of a large carnivore population. Packer's work has examined lion social organization, cooperation, territoriality, reproduction, genetics, population dynamics and interactions with other carnivores.<ref name="Website-1" /><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Packer |first=Craig |date=2019-07-02 |title=The African Lion: A Long History of Interdisciplinary Research |journal=Frontiers in Ecology and Evolution |language=English |publisher=Frontiers |volume=7 |article-number=259 |doi=10.3389/fevo.2019.00259  |doi-access=free|bibcode=2019FrEEv...7..259P |issn=2296-701X}}</ref>

In 1986, Packer established the Lion Research Center at the [[University of Minnesota]], described by the university as the first research center dedicated to the study of lions. The center has brought together researchers from fields including ecology, genetics and virology to study lion biology and conservation.<ref name=":4" />

Packer's research has also examined disease in lion populations.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2009-11-01 |title=Severe Droughts Trigger Disease, Lion Die-Offs |url=https://www.voanews.com/a/a-13-2008-07-08-voa27/405291.html |access-date=2026-10-20 |website=Voice of America |language=en}}</ref> His work with collaborators investigated outbreaks of [[canine distemper]] in [[Panthera leo melanochaita|Serengeti lions]] and the effects of environmental conditions on disease dynamics.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Morell |first=Virginia |title=The Killer Cat Virus That Doesn't Kill Cats |url=https://www.discovermagazine.com/the-killer-cat-virus-that-doesnt-kill-cats-11834 |website=[[Discover Magazine]]}}</ref> Other research has addressed the genetics of lion populations,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Miller |first1=Susan M. |last2=Druce |first2=Dave J. |last3=Dalton |first3=Desiré L. |last4=Harper |first4=Cindy K. |last5=Kotze |first5=Antoinette |last6=Packer |first6=Craig |last7=Slotow |first7=Rob |last8=Bloomer |first8=Paulette |date=2020-02-01 |title=Genetic rescue of an isolated African lion population |url=https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/85076466448 |journal=Conservation Genetics |volume=21 |issue=1 |pages=41–53 |doi=10.1007/s10592-019-01231-y |bibcode=2020ConG...21...41M |issn=1566-0621}}</ref> reproductive strategies,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Packer |first1=Craig |last2=Pusey |first2=Anne E. |date=1983 |title=Male takeovers and female reproductive parameters: A simulation of oestrous synchrony in lions (Panthera leo) |url=https://www.scopus.com/pages/publications/0001041677 |journal=Animal Behaviour |volume=31 |issue=2 |pages=334–340 |doi=10.1016/S0003-3472(83)80051-7 |bibcode=1983AnBeh..31..334P |issn=0003-3472}}</ref> predator–prey relationships and the effects of trophy hunting on lion populations.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Packer |first1=C. |last2=Brink |first2=H. |last3=Kissui |first3=B. M. |last4=Maliti |first4=H. |last5=Kushnir |first5=H. |last6=Caro |first6=T. |date=2011 |title=Effects of trophy hunting on lion and leopard populations in Tanzania |journal=Conservation Biology: The Journal of the Society for Conservation Biology |volume=25 |issue=1 |pages=142–153 |doi=10.1111/j.1523-1739.2010.01576.x |issn=1523-1739 |pmid=20825444}}</ref>

=== Snapshot Serengeti and citizen science ===
Packer was involved in establishing [[Snapshot Serengeti]], a large-scale camera-trap project in [[Serengeti National Park]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Harlan |first=Becky |date=2014-11-26 |title=Hidden Cameras Reveal the Secret Life of the Serengeti |url=https://www.nationalgeographic.com/photography/article/hidden-cameras-reveal-the-secret-life-of-the-serengeti |access-date=2026-10-20 |website=Photography |language=en}}</ref> Beginning in 2010, researchers deployed 225 camera traps across approximately 1,125 square kilometres to record wildlife interactions. Members of the public helped classify the resulting photographs through a [[citizen science]] platform. The project generated data on dozens of mammal species and was subsequently developed into the broader Snapshot Safari initiative.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Swanson |first1=Alexandra |last2=Kosmala |first2=Margaret |last3=Lintott |first3=Chris |last4=Simpson |first4=Robert |last5=Smith |first5=Arfon |last6=Packer |first6=Craig |date=2015-06-09 |title=Snapshot Serengeti, high-frequency annotated camera trap images of 40 mammalian species in an African savanna |journal=Scientific Data |language=en |publisher=Nature Publishing Group |volume=2 |issue=1 |pages=150026 |doi=10.1038/sdata.2015.26  |doi-access=free|pmid=26097743 |pmc=4460915 |bibcode=2015NatSD...250026S |issn=2052-4463}}</ref>

=== Conservation and human–wildlife conflict ===
In 2014, Tanzanian authorities barred him from returning to the country after he made statements criticizing corruption in the country's government-run trophy-hunting industry.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2015-09-16 |title=This Lion Expert Was Banned From Tanzania for Exposing Corruption |url=https://www.nationalgeographic.com/history/article/150916-book-talk-simon-worrall-craig-packer-lions-serengeti-tanzania-trophy-hunting-africa-conservation |access-date=2026-10-20 |website=History |language=en}}</ref> Packer discussed the episode and its relationship to lion conservation in his 2015 book ''Lions in the Balance''.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Barbier |first=iris |title=Lions in the Balance: Can hunting save the kings of the jungle? |url=https://www.newscientist.com/article/2052462-lions-in-the-balance-can-hunting-save-the-kings-of-the-jungle/ |website=New Scientist}}</ref>

Packer has worked with conservation organizations on human–wildlife coexistence, livestock management, predator conservation and grassland restoration. He became Scientific Director of the Mara Predator Conservation Program in Kenya in 2019 and continues to work on lion conservation in the [[Maasai Mara]] ecosystem.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Savage |first=Jess |date=2023-03-29 |title=Protecting predators and facilitating large scale food drives. |url=https://governorscamp.com/blog/protecting-predators-and-facilitating-large-scale-food-drives/ |access-date=2026-10-20 |website=The Governors Camp |language=en-US}}</ref>

His recent research has included the relationship between tourism and lion conservation in the [[Maasai Mara]], human-driven landscapes of fear, lion population connectivity and human–carnivore conflict. Packer has also been involved with Savannas Forever Tanzania, an organization concerned with conservation and [[sustainable development]] in rural Africa. His current research includes efforts to restore degraded grasslands and develop livestock-grazing practices that reduce pressure on wildlife habitat.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Mogensen |first1=Niels |last2=Packer |first2=Craig |last3=Svenning |first3=Jens-Christian |last4=Amoke |first4=Irene |last5=Buitenwerf |first5=Robert |date=2026 |title=Balancing benefits and burdens: Tourist camps and lion conservation in the Maasai Mara |journal=Conservation Science and Practice |language=en |volume=8 |issue=2 |article-number=e70210 |doi=10.1111/csp2.70210 |doi-access=free |bibcode=2026ConSP...870210M |issn=2578-4854}}</ref>

=== Selected recent research ===
In 2023 he co-authored research on the ecological and socio-political fragility of African lion populations and a study of the effects of humans as a "[[Superpredator|super predator]]" on South African [[Savanna|savannas]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Zanette |first1=Liana Y. |last2=Frizzelle |first2=Nikita R. |last3=Clinchy |first3=Michael |last4=Peel |first4=Michael J.S. |last5=Keller |first5=Carson B. |last6=Huebner |first6=Sarah E. |last7=Packer |first7=Craig |date=2023 |title=Fear of the human "super predator" pervades the South African savanna |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0960982223011697 |journal=Current Biology |language=en |volume=33 |issue=21 |pages=4689–4696.e4 |doi=10.1016/j.cub.2023.08.089 |pmid=37802052 |bibcode=2023CBio...33E4689Z |hdl=11299/276657 |hdl-access=free }}</ref>

In 2024 he co-authored studies of [[density dependence]] in [[Panthera leo melanochaita|Serengeti lion]] demography, human–lion conflict in Namibia and social ageing in wild African lions. He also co-authored research on the interaction of competition and facilitation in grazing succession among Serengeti herbivores.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Conquet |first1=Eva |last2=Paniw |first2=Maria |last3=Borrego |first3=Natalia |last4=Nater |first4=Chloé R. |last5=Packer |first5=Craig |last6=Ozgul |first6=Arpat |date=2024 |title=Multifaceted density dependence: Social structure and seasonality effects on Serengeti lion demography |url=https://besjournals.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/1365-2656.14158 |journal=Journal of Animal Ecology |language=en |volume=93 |issue=10 |pages=1493–1509 |doi=10.1111/1365-2656.14158 |pmid=39080877 |bibcode=2024JAnEc..93.1493C |issn=0021-8790|hdl=10261/387354 |hdl-access=free }}</ref>

In 2025 his publications included research on [[oxytocin]] and dominance relationships in captive female lions, genomic erosion in the [[Ngorongoro Crater]] lion population, cooperative hunting and social dynamics in carnivores, tourism and lion conservation in the [[Maasai Mara]], and the effects of livestock intensification on wildlife.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Burkhart |first1=Jessica C. |last2=Guthmann |first2=Abby |last3=DuBois |first3=Evianne M. |last4=Heilbronner |first4=Sarah R. |last5=Packer |first5=Craig |date=2025-07-02 |title=Oxytocin reduces asymmetries in dominance relationships between pairs of captive female lions |journal=Scientific Reports |language=en |publisher=Nature Publishing Group |volume=15 |issue=1 |pages=23366 |doi=10.1038/s41598-025-04276-x  |doi-access=free|pmid=40603881 |pmc=12223073 |bibcode=2025NatSR..1523366B |issn=2045-2322}}</ref>

In 2026 he published research on human-driven landscapes of fear affecting Africa's largest terrestrial predator and on long-term social dynamics among African lions. He also co-authored work on biodiversity and economic development and on human–wildlife conflict.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Mogensen |first1=Niels |last2=Packer |first2=Craig |last3=Svenning |first3=Jens-Christian |last4=Sankan |first4=Kasaine |last5=Buitenwerf |first5=Robert |date=2026 |title=Human-driven landscapes of fear for Africa's largest terrestrial predator in human-used conservation landscapes |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0006320725006366 |journal=Biological Conservation |language=en |volume=313 |article-number=111599 |doi=10.1016/j.biocon.2025.111599 |bibcode=2026BCons.31311599M }}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
Packer received a [[Guggenheim Fellowship]] in 1990<ref>{{Cite web |title=*NEW DATE & TIME* Lion Conservation on a Crowded Continent - Craig Packer |url=http://www.lectures.iastate.edu/lecture/44667 |access-date=2026-10-20 |website=Iowa State Lectures Program |language=en}}</ref> and was awarded the [[John Burroughs Medal]] in 1995 for ''Into Africa''.<ref name=":3" /> In 1997 he was named a Distinguished McKnight University Professor at the [[University of Minnesota]]. He was elected a Fellow of the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] in 2003.<ref name="gfellow">{{cite web|url=https://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/craig-packer/|title=Craig Packer|work=[[John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation]]|access-date=April 21, 2017}}</ref><ref name="mcprof">{{cite web|url=http://www.scholarswalk.umn.edu/awards/mcknight/mcknight_distinguished.html|title=Distinguished McKnight University Professors|work=[[University of Minnesota]]|access-date=April 21, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170512013440/http://www.scholarswalk.umn.edu/awards/mcknight/mcknight_distinguished.html|archive-date=May 12, 2017}}</ref><ref name="amacad">{{cite web|url=https://www.amacad.org/content/system/search.aspx?s=Craig+Packer|title=Professor Craig Packer|work=[[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]]|access-date=April 21, 2017}}{{Dead link|date=July 2020 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> 

In 2017 Packer received the Wildlife Conservation Award from the [[Cincinnati Zoo and Botanical Garden]] for his work on lions in the Serengeti.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lab |first=M. S. D. |date=2017-05-04 |title=Cincinnati Zoo Celebrates 25 Years of Celebrating Wildlife Conservation Achievement |url=https://cincinnatizoo.org/cincinnati-zoo-celebrates-25-years-of-celebrating-wildlife-conservation-achievement/ |access-date=2026-03-30 |website=Cincinnati Zoo & Botanical Garden |language=en-US}}</ref> In 2018 he received the Dawkins Conservation Award from [[Balliol College, Oxford]].<ref name=":4" /> In 2019 he was elected a Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]].<ref name=":0" />

In 2013, Snapshot Serengeti was selected as one of the "Top Ten" citizen-science projects by ''The Ecologist''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Be part of a Serengeti soap opera |url=https://atlasofthefuture.org/project/snapshot-serengeti/ |access-date=2026-03-30 |website=Atlas of the Future}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://video.nationalgeographic.com/video/til/160309-craig-packer-female-lions-find-black-manes-sexy|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160312180201/http://video.nationalgeographic.com/video/til/160309-craig-packer-female-lions-find-black-manes-sexy|archive-date=March 12, 2016|title=Today I Learned: Female Lions Are Attracted to Black Manes|work=[[National Geographic Society|National Geographic]]|date=2016|access-date=April 21, 2017}}</ref><ref name="IUCN">{{Cite iucn | author = Bauer, H. | author2 = Packer, C. | author3 = Funston, P.F. | author4 = Henschel, P. | author5 = Nowell, K. | title = ''Panthera leo'' | year= 2016 | errata = 2017 | article-number = e.T15951A115130419 | date = 2016 | doi = 10.2305/IUCN.UK.2016-3.RLTS.T15951A107265605.en }}</ref><ref name="natgeobio" /> 

== Personal life ==
Packer is married to Susan James<ref name=":1" /> and has two children from his previous marriage to [[Anne E. Pusey|Anne Pusey]]: Jonathan (1987), who is a pulmonologist in Sacramento, California and Catherine (1984), who holds an [[Master of Public Health|MPH]] from Johns Hopkins.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wieder |first=Ben |date=2011-06-26 |title=At Duke, an Evolutionary Anthropologist Plumbs Jane Goodall's Research Trove |url=https://www.chronicle.com/article/at-duke-an-evolutionary-anthropologist-plumbs-jane-goodalls-research-trove/ |access-date=2026-04-16 |website=The Chronicle of Higher Education |language=en}}</ref> He has two grandchildren, Sienna and Felix.
